title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. A is a commutative ring, S = Spec(A), and C is an A-linear category: the Hom-sets are A-modules and composition is A-bilinear. C need not be additive. For each A-algebra A', Grothendieck defines C_{A'}: same objects as C, with Hom_{C_{A'}}(X,Y) = Hom_C(X,Y) ⊗_A A'. This gives a fibred category of linear categories over the ringed site of affine S-schemes.

When it is a stack. Grothendieck notes it is almost never a stack on this big site, even for the Zariski topology. Restricted to the small affine Zariski site of S (affine opens Spec A_f), it often is a stack, denoted C (underlined). C is then called 'localisable sur A'. Concretely:
- Hom-sets glue, which is automatic, since Hom ⊗ A_f is a quasi-coherent sheaf.
- Objects glue: given X_i in C_{A_{f_i}} and isomorphisms over the overlaps satisfying the cocycle condition, there is a global object of C inducing them.

Consequence (a). Let R be an A-algebra, not necessarily commutative, and X an object with an A-linear R-action. Let P be a right R-module that is Zariski-locally on S isomorphic to R_d (R as a right module).
- The tensor product P ⊗_R X exists in C. It represents Y ↦ Hom_R(P, Hom_C(X,Y)). Locally it is represented by X, and the stack property glues these representatives.
- If R → End_C(X) is bijective, the functor P ↦ P ⊗_R X, from the category P(R) of such modules to C, is fully faithful.
- Its essential image (handwritten addition) is the set of objects X' 'locally isomorphic to X over A'. The inverse is X' ↦ Hom_C(X, X'), a right End(X)-module.
- Equivalently, the forms of X in C are classified by H^1(S_Zar, sheaf of units of R) = H^1(S_Zar, Aut X), the usual twisting principle.

Consequence (b). If C is additive, the stack C (underlined) is a stack of additive A-linear categories.
- For P locally free of finite type over R, P ⊗_R X exists.
- If R = End X, the functor P ↦ P ⊗_R X is fully faithful.
- Its essential image (next page) is the objects locally isomorphic to some X^n.
- The NB on the next page says Karoubianity with P finitely generated projective suffices.

Purpose (title 'Localisation pour les variétés abéliennes'). This is the categorical framework for the arithmetic of abelian varieties up to 'genus'.
- Take C = abelian varieties over a field and A = Z. Then X, X' are 'apparentés' (same genus) iff they become isomorphic in C_{Z_(p)} for all p, i.e. iff there are isogenies of degree prime to each p.
- The theory identifies a genus class with invertible (or locally free) modules over the order End(X). This is the Deuring correspondence for supersingular elliptic curves, abstracted; the next page introduces 'catégories de Deuring'.
- Its higher-rank version is the classification of abelian varieties locally isomorphic to E^n by modules over End(E).
- For abelian varieties, localisability amounts to gluing local Z_(p)-modifications, i.e. lattice modifications by isogenies. Over finite fields this is naturally linked to Tate's isogeny theorem, Hom ⊗ Z_ℓ = Hom_Gal(T_ℓ, T_ℓ), though the page does not say so.
errors: In (b) the typescript reads 'si R → End_C(X)' without the verb; 'est bijectif' is clearly intended, as in (a).
The bijectivity hypothesis R ≅ End_C(X) in (a) was missing in the typescript and added by hand. Without it, full faithfulness fails: Hom(P⊗X, P'⊗X) = Hom_R(P, P' ⊗_R End(X)).
For (b), the stack property for objects is needed to glue the local X^n. The NB on the next page correctly notes that, for P projective of finite type, Karoubianity suffices without localisability.
Minor: 'catégories [A-]linéaires' — the A was struck; the fibre over A' is A'-linear, so the correction is right.

ideas.what: Base change of a linear category, C_{A'} with Hom ⊗_A A', viewed as a fibred category over affine S-schemes; 'localisable' means it is a stack on the small affine Zariski site
ideas.modern_name: Zariski descent / stackification of a linear category over Spec A; local–global principle for objects of an A-linear category
ideas.usually_credited_to: No standard name; related ideas are in Giraud (Cohomologie non abélienne, 1971) and genus theory of lattices (Eichler, Fröhlich)

ideas.what: Twisting X by locally free rank-one right R-modules; forms of X classified by torsors under End(X)^× on S_Zar; equivalence between invertible R-modules and objects locally isomorphic to X
ideas.modern_name: Serre tensor construction M ⊗_R X; nonabelian H^1 classification of forms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (tensor construction, ca. 1967 / Serre–Tate); Giraud for nonabelian H^1

ideas.what: Objects locally isomorphic to X^n correspond to locally free right End(X)-modules of finite type (additive case), with a Karoubian variant for projective modules
ideas.modern_name: Module-theoretic description of abelian varieties isogenous to a power of a given one (Kani; Jordan–Keeton–Poonen–Rains–Shepherd-Barron–Tate 2018)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Waterhouse (1969), Kani (2011), JKPRST (2018); Deuring (1941) for the supersingular rank-one case

ideas.what: 'Apparentés' = locally isomorphic over A, i.e. same genus; the full subcategory of a genus is localisable and is a 'catégorie de Deuring' (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Genus of an abelian variety; Deuring correspondence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring; genus language for abelian varieties appears later (e.g. Kirschmer–Narbonne–Ritzenthaler–Robert-type works on polarized genera)

missed.claim: An abstract categorical formulation, as Zariski stacks of linear categories over Spec Z, of the Deuring correspondence and of genus theory for abelian varieties. Objects of a genus correspond to locally free modules over End(X), with the class set as H^1 of the unit sheaf. This anticipates by decades the equivalence of JKPRST/Kani between abelian varieties locally isomorphic to E^n and modules over End(E).
missed.quote: son image essentielle est formée des X'∈Ob C qui sont "localement isomorphes à X" sur A
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives a uniform base-change/descent criterion ('localisable') under which Serre-tensor-type equivalences hold. It could unify the various ad hoc proofs (supersingular, ordinary, CM, power-of-elliptic-curve cases) and suggests asking exactly when categories of abelian varieties or motives are localisable over Z.

missed.claim: The question of when C is localisable for abelian varieties (or motives) is left open here; the next page also notes that localisability over Spec(R), rather than Spec(A), is not proved.
missed.quote: Notre raisonnement ne prouve pas que Mod(R,C) est localisable sur R i.e. sur Spec(R)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Localisability over the centre of End(X) would give finer genus/class-group descriptions, e.g. over orders in CM fields. Its relation to Tate's isogeny theorem as the gluing input seems not to be formulated in this categorical form in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The individual tools (twisting, descent, Serre tensor construction) are standard. But an abstract 'localisable A-linear category' framework explicitly aimed at abelian varieties and 'Deuring categories', anticipating the genus/module equivalences of Waterhouse, Kani and JKPRST, is an unpublished and essentially uncredited perspective.
